captions.text: Recap of chapter 24: a long chat loses its oldest messages, with no error.
Trim keeps you in budget by choosing what to lose.
Summarise looked perfect on a short test.
On a long chat it wasn't. Summaries lose the facts that matter.
Today's black box: facts about a person that outlive the conversation.
Let's open it. But first, watch a new session forget someone.
Meet Hana, who's made up for this chapter. She tells the agent her locker number. Then we ask twice.
The only difference is history. Predict: what will the new session say?
Same session: 212. New session: it has no idea.
5 of 5 against 0 of 5. No error. The messages list simply ended with the run.
The obvious fix: when the chat ends, ask the model for the facts. 36 messages, 12 facts.
10 of 12, and never NONE. Better than we expected, on this chat.
But Marek's flu isn't about Hana. And her question became a rule: "Can carry leave over".
And if the program dies first, nothing's saved. So decide message by message. But who decides?
Three setups. Code checks every message. Or a remember tool saves the model's words.
Or the same tool, and the code saves what she said. Predict: which remembers most?
Code checks: 39 of 60, nothing unwanted. The model's words: 50. Her words: 59.
Ignore the Memory row for now. Code checks never kept the knee, allergy, trip or badge.
It's one chat. Treat that gap as something to explain, not as a ranking.
So read the notes. Unwanted ones are mostly noise, about other people and deliveries.
But look: "The flapjack contains nuts." Hana only asked if it did. 1 run in 5.
Rewriting lets the model invent. Her own words can't. That's the difference, not the count.
A quieter danger. Save the model's line, and tell it to copy numbers exactly.
Your locker number is 5093, in all 5 runs. That's her staff number.
It copied 212 exactly, and dropped the word locker. The label was the fact.
Thursdays lost "can't". Monday became a day off. Her sentence had both parts.
Be fair to code checks. Is it the rule, "A question is not a fact"? Predict.
Removing the rule hardly moved it. "Even in passing" picked all 12 facts.
So one phrase did much of that gap. We wrote it after reading these failures, so it's a direction.
Here's the finished class. The model gets a tool called remember.
Read it closely. It never uses fact. The model's words can't reach the file.
self.latest is what she just said. A before_model hook keeps it up to date.
append keeps the notes oldest first. Remember that line.
The line above takes out a repeat, so it moves to the end. The newest note wins.
Write a temporary file, then os.replace swaps it in, in one step. A crash can't leave half a file.
A short session with Memory. Predict: which messages get saved?
It's a JSON file you can open. Her words, and the date.
But "Can't do Thursdays" wasn't saved. No error. That's the price of letting the model decide.
A new program, and all it has is the file. Predict: which questions will it get?
Locker 5 of 5, against 0 of 5 before. Old Mill came along in her words.
Thursdays: 0 of 5. It can't know what was never saved.
The finished class on all 36 messages, five times.
57 of 60, with 2 or 3 unwanted notes, every one in her words. Too close to 59 to rank.
Now facts change. Hana moves branch, and both notes stay. 60 notes. Predict: what goes stale?
In order: 20 of 20, nothing stale, at 12 notes and at 60.
Backwards: 10 stale. Shuffled: 2, and every stale answer had the old note last.
Dates didn't clearly help. And they cost more tokens.
Replacing took 35 calls, missed 2 of 4 changes, and lost the old branch: before 0 of 5.
So order is a fact your code already knows. And 60 notes is under 1,000 tokens, so no search.
Two weak spots. She says something, changes it, then says it again. Predict the answer.
The repeat moved to the end, and 4 of 5 runs gave 212. One asked her to clear it up.
With Thursdays the order is right too, and every answer calls it a change or a mix-up. Order helps. It doesn't decide.
And a note can be "Please save that". Not in this run, but in 2 of our 15.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and complete the five TODOs.
You've finished when you see 5 passed.
A new session has only what you give it, so write notes to disk.
The model makes the call. The code keeps the facts and the order.
We tested one person and one 7B model. Measure yours.
